title: [Màj] Multiples vulnérabilités dans PHP (21 octobre 2026)
text:
Bulletin d'alerte du CERT-FR

Json

Objet : [Màj] Multiples vulnérabilités dans PHP

Gestion du document

Référence
CERTFR-2026-ALE-014

Titre
[Màj] Multiples vulnérabilités dans PHP

Date de la première version21 octobre 2026

Date de la dernière version21 octobre 2026

Source(s)
Communication de PHP du 20 octobre 2026Bulletin de sécurité PHP du 21 octobre 2026Bulletin de sécurité PHP du 21 octobre 2026Bulletin de sécurité PHP du 21 octobre 2026Bulletin de sécurité PHP du 21 octobre 2026

Une gestion de version détaillée se trouve à la fin de ce document.

Risque

Exécution de code arbitraire à distance

Systèmes affectés

PHP toutes versions 5.x

PHP toutes versions 6.x

PHP toutes versions 7.x

PHP toutes versions 8.0.x

PHP toutes versions 8.1.x

PHP versions 8.2.x antérieures à 8.2.35

PHP versions 8.3.x antérieures à 8.3.36

PHP versions 8.4.x antérieures à 8.4.27

PHP versions 8.5.x antérieures à 8.5.12

Résumé
[Mise à jours du 21 octobre 2026]
Les correctifs de sécurité sont disponibles sur le site de l'éditeur. PHP indique que les vulnérabilités CVE-2026-109618 et CVE-2026-109619 permettent à un attaquant de provoquer une exécution de code arbitraire à distance.
[Publication Initiale]
Le 20 octobre 2026, PHP a publié une communication concernant deux vulnérabilités critiques. L'éditeur annonce la disponibilité des correctifs de sécurité pour le 21 octobre 2026 à 16h00 heure de Paris (14h00 UTC).
Pour les versions de PHP 5.x, 6.x, 7.x, 8.0.x et 8.1.x , dont l'éditeur n'assure plus le support.
Le CERT-FR recommande d'isoler les équipements affectés puis de procéder à la migration vers une version maintenue et avec les derniers correctifs de sécurité dès publication du correctif éditeur.

Contournement provisoire
Ces contournements provisoires ne sont pas qualifiés par le CERT-FR :

appliquer la configuration suivante dans le fichier php.ini :

session.upload_progress.enabled = Off

Si le processus PHP-FPM s'exécute, il sera aussi nécessaire de modifier la variable php_admin_flag comme suit :
php_admin_flag[session.upload_progress.enabled] = off

La conséquence sera la désactivation de la fonctionnalité PHP upload-progress. Il est à noter que cette mesure d'atténuation ne réduit la surface d'attaque que contre l'une des deux vulnérabilités.

bloquer toutes requêtes HTTP dont l'en-tête contient un Content-Type positionné à la valeur multipart.
Si le blocage ne peut être appliqué, il est fortement recommandé d'appliquer une politique de supervision pour ce type de requête.

Ces mesures peuvent être réalisées au niveau d'un pare-feu applicatif (Web Application Firewall).
Solutions
Se référer au bulletin de sécurité de l'éditeur pour l'obtention des correctifs (cf. section Documentation).

title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
text:
Security Advisory 2026-018

Release Date:
21-10-2026 15:20:18

Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP

Download

Download PDF

Download MARKDOWN

Download JSON

History:21/10/2026 --- v1.0 -- Initial publication21/10/2026 --- v1.1 -- Updates with additional informationSummaryOn 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP [1]. Public reports indicated that these vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution [2,3].The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 [4]. Both vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities.CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.Technical DetailsThe vulnerability CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w), with a CVSS score of 9.2, allows remote code execution through memory corruption during out-of-memory (OOM) handling [4,6]. PHP enforces its user-configurable memory_limit by using longjmp() to abort any request that exceeds the limit, which raises an OOM error. This can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialised, for example while parsing a form-based file upload. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid and try to free memory that was never initialised. That memory may still contain data from earlier allocations controlled by the attacker.The vulnerability CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp), with a CVSS score of 9.2, allows remote code execution through stale global state [4,7]. Internal state owned by a request can survive after its backing memory has been freed, for example after a fatal error. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialisation resets it.Every PHP installation that serves web requests is at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. The PHP team considers mod_php the highest-risk setup. A demonstrated exploit shows that one unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs [4].Affected ProductsPHP 8.5 versions prior to 8.5.12PHP 8.4 versions prior to 8.4.27PHP 8.3 versions prior to 8.3.36PHP 8.2 versions prior to 8.2.35End-of-life branches (PHP 8.1 and older), which no longer receive updates from the PHP project [4]Many commercial and open-source products use PHP as a backend technology - these could be also affected, even if they do not directly expose a PHP installation. CERT-EU recommends consulting the NCSC-NL GitHub repository to identify third-party software that embeds PHP and may be impacted by these vulnerabilities [5]. CERT-EU strongly recommends updating all affected PHP installations as soon as possible to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 [4].Distribution packages: Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance. Check with your vendor for updated packages.End-of-life versions (PHP 8.1 and older): Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor or upgrade to a supported version. Because of the severity, the PHP security team has also published minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for organisations that build from source or have no LTS vendor.rpms.remirepo.net users: This volunteer-maintained repository will not have updates on release day. The PHP team urges users to switch to distribution packages or build from source.Where immediate patching is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing resources from public networks until the fix is applied and verified.Temporary […]

title: EDRi celebrates Global Encryption Day 2026
text:
Skip to content

Close

Search

How would you best describe that thing you're looking for?

On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.
A recent survey conducted by CDT Europe shows that across several European countries (France, Sweden, Poland, and Ireland), people consistently oppose measures that would compromise encrypted communication platforms. In France, 92% of respondents agree they have the right to have private conversations online, while the figure goes to 94% in Poland, 88% in Sweden and 93% in Ireland.
Encryption is great for protecting the way our messages travel on the internet. Through “end to end encryption”, anyone can make sure that the content of an online conversation can not be intruded upon, not even the server that facilitates the transmission.
This year, we have coordinated several campaign actions to celebrate encryption.
1. Raising awareness in European Capitals through LED “Encryption trucks” driving around Paris, Berlin and Dublin and a metro poster campaign in Prague.
To visibilise people’s support for encryption, we partnered with the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement and Digitale Gesellschaft who are in the streets today, talking to people and press about the “Encryption trucks” and the importance of encryption. In Prague, our partner Iure has been supporting the Metro Posters campaign for the past weeks.
2. Working across silos with groups promoting gender justice, and sex workers rights in the digitalised society.
In the case of women defenders, land defenders from indigenous groups, racial justice activists, sex workers defenders and defenders of migrants, unsafe communications can have life or death consequences. For human rights defenders, secure and trusted communication is often a matter of physical safety and democratic organising.
For 21 October 2026, we have partnered with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement (France) to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. Check ESWA’s Instagram video and
3. Visibilising the testimonials of activists from Privacy Camp and across Europe
During 14th edition of Privacy Camp gathering that happened recently in Brussels, EDRi asked a few participants why encryption mattered for them. The people we interviewed came from a variety of causes: those fighting for a healthy European civic space, and for digital rights in Netherlands, Portugal and Germany. More, we asked EDRi’s over 35.000 supporters why encryption mattered to them too. Their answers inspired us to post some of them, and we will post them during the next couple of weeks. Check the content on EDRi’s social media channels – on Instagram , Mastodon or LinkedIn.
4. Connecting with global experts to advocate for encryption
During the Global Encryption Summit taking place at 4pm CET, EDRi’s expert Chloé Berthélémy will join a panel in an event organised by Internet Society, the Center for Democracy and Technology, Mozilla, and Global Partners Digital.
What is the threat to encryption?
Europol and law enforcement are pushing to legalise hacking methods that weaken encryption. These methods rely on ordering a service provider (those who develop or maintain the software, computer system, network, or electronic device) to build vulnerabilities in their systems. With this demand, state actors want to enable the police or intelligence agencies to have access to our data and break encryption. Client-side scanning (scanning of all content such as text,images, videos, etc. on a device or shared in a communication channel) is a method proposed under the EU CSA Regulation. title: CVE-2026-96640 - Pillow PDF append accepts malformed shared page-tree DAG causing resource exhaustion
text:
8.2

HIGH
CVSS 4.0

CVE-2026-96640
Pillow PDF append accepts malformed shared page-tree DAG causing resource exhaustion

Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.1.0 until 13.0.0, PdfParser.linearize_page_tree() in src/PIL/PdfParser.py treats a PDF /Pages graph as a tree without tracking duplicate indirect references. When Image.save(..., format="PDF", append=True) processes an attacker-controlled existing PDF whose /Kids arrays repeatedly reference the same child /Pages node, Pillow expands the shared subtree as distinct pages. A compact malformed PDF can therefore create exponentially many page references and consume disproportionate CPU before the append completes. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

title: CVE-2026-96639 - Pillow multi-frame loaders can reuse stale native image storage after mode transitions
text:
9.8

CRITICAL
CVSS 3.1

CVE-2026-96639
Pillow multi-frame loaders can reuse stale native image storage after mode transitions

Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 11.0.0 until 13.0.0, multi-frame loaders can retain an ImagingCore allocation created for a narrow frame mode while a later frame of the same dimensions changes the logical mode and decoder tiles to wider RGB or CMYK data. ImageFile.load_prepare() reuses the stale native storage because _im is non-null without verifying that its mode and size still match. Crafted PSD, MPO, DCX, or MIC frame transitions can then write wider pixels into the narrow allocation, causing native out-of-bounds writes and crashes. The MPO path can also cause a native over-read and, in demonstrated runtime-specific profiles, command execution. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

CVE-2026-29001
TastyIgniter 4.4.5 PHP Object Injection via Settings Deserialization

text:

CVE-2026-114143
toml-node: Quadratic-complexity DoS via long dotted keys or table paths in toml.parse()

toml-node is a TOML parser for Node.js and the browser. Prior to 5.0.1, toml.parse() repeatedly slices and rejoins every path prefix in lib/compiler.js while processing long dotted keys, table headers, array-of-tables headers, and inline-table keys in assign(), deepRef(), and setNestedKey(). The resulting quadratic work can block the Node.js event loop for several seconds, and sufficiently long paths can terminate the process through memory exhaustion. The maxDepth option does not limit key-segment count and therefore does not mitigate this path. This issue is fixed in version 5.0.1.

title: CVE-2026-114142 - toml-node: Prototype pollution: parsing a TOML document can write to Object.prototype
text:
8.8

HIGH
CVSS 4.0

CVE-2026-114142
toml-node: Prototype pollution: parsing a TOML document can write to Object.prototype

toml-node is a TOML parser for Node.js and the browser. Prior to 5.0.1, toml.parse() can write attacker-controlled properties to Object.prototype because quoteDottedString() in lib/compiler.js produces the same bookkeeping string for distinct quoted key paths, allowing addTableArray() to clear another key's guard. The assign() path then descends through an unowned Date value without applying the owned-container check and can reach the prototype chain. Objects created elsewhere in the process can inherit the injected property. This issue is fixed in version 5.0.1.

nbconvert: File write via path traversal in cell output filenames

The nbconvert tool, jupyter nbconvert, converts Jupyter notebooks to various other formats via Jinja templates. From 5.4.0 until 7.17.2, ExtractOutputPreprocessor in nbconvert/preprocessors/extractoutput.py joins the attacker-controlled cell output metadata filename to output_files_dir without limiting the result to the intended directory. Running the notebook cell again replaces the malicious output metadata, but merely converting the supplied notebook does not. This issue is fixed in version 7.17.2.

CVE-2026-114135 - Jupyter Server: Gateway WebSocket handler bypasses kernel execute authorization
text:
8.8

HIGH
CVSS 3.1

CVE-2026-114135
Jupyter Server: Gateway WebSocket handler bypasses kernel execute authorization

Jupyter Server is the backend for Jupyter web applications. From 2.0.0 until 2.6.0, enabling GatewayClient.url replaced the normal KernelWebsocketHandler with WebSocketChannelsHandler, which authenticated the user but did not call authorizer.is_authorized(...) for the execute action on the kernels resource. A restricted authenticated user could therefore open an upstream kernel channel and obtain kernel execution despite the configured Authorizer denying that action, exposing data and credentials available to the kernel and permitting modification or disruption of the kernel environment. The default gateway configuration is fixed in version 2.6.0. In 2.6.0 and later, the same authorization bypass remains possible when a deployment manually registers the deprecated jupyter_server.gateway.handlers module, because its handler still omits the configured kernel-execute authorization decision.

title: CrowdStrike Protects Customers from Threats Delivered via PHP2Shell
text:
CrowdStrike Protects Customers from Threats Delivered via PHP2Shell
Two critical memory-corruption RCE vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 have been disclosed in core PHP.

October 21, 2026
•

Amit Serper
•

From The Front Lines

Two critical memory-corruption remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, collectively dubbed PHP2Shell, have been disclosed in core PHP, the underlying engine powering a vast portion of the web. The CrowdStrike Falcon® platform provides out-of-the-box visibility and detection coverage for post-exploitation activities of both vulnerabilities.
Tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 (Critical) and are classified as CWE-824: Access of Uninitialized Pointer. Both allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary system commands on an affected web server over HTTP.
The two issues share a single root cause. When PHP encounters a fatal condition (exhausting its configured memory_limit, exceeding the maximum execution time, or losing the client connection), it does not return an error up the call stack. It raises a fatal error and uses longjmp() to abandon the current execution context outright, aborting the request. Any C function caught midway through building a data structure is simply discarded: no destructors run, no bookkeeping is rolled back, and nothing records that the structure is incomplete. PHP then proceeds into an otherwise ordinary cleanup sequence that assumes every structure is in a consistent state.
The two CVEs describe where that assumption breaks:
CVE-2026-109618 (RCE via out-of-memory) covers contexts that leave request memory uninitialized. A data structure is marked as containing an entry before the memory backing that entry is allocated; when the allocation is the one that crosses the memory limit, the entry is left holding stale heap data. The failing request's own cleanup routine then reads and branches on those bytes.CVE-2026-109619 (RCE via fatal errors) covers contexts that leave global state invalid. A module-level global still points into the per-request heap that shutdown has already freed, and still reports its operation as active. A subsequent request handled by the same worker process reads or branches on that freed memory.
In both cases, the attacker controls the trigger and, critically, the data that PHP ultimately misinterprets. CrowdStrike has verified end-to-end that a single anonymous POST request can cause an Apache mod_php worker to launch a shell process and execute an attacker-specified command, with no authentication, no session, and no vulnerable application code involved.
What elevates these vulnerabilities is their placement in the execution stack. PHP parses incoming request data before extensions are initialized and before a single line of application code is compiled, so exploitation is independent of what the server hosts. A meticulously maintained application is exposed to precisely the same degree as a neglected one. The attack is also remarkably quiet: The worker process does not crash, the server returns a standard HTTP 200 response, and application logs record nothing unusual.
In our testing, we developed an exploit code that operated consistently across x86-64 and ARM architectures, remained reliable across worker restarts, and on ARM-based hosts, which are increasingly common in cloud fleets, defeated Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) using only HTTP requests.
Technical Details
The Shared Root Cause: longjmp() Without Unwinding
Both vulnerabilities live in Zend, the engine at the heart of PHP. Zend is the C implementation that compiles PHP source into bytecode, executes it in a virtual machine, and manages everything the language needs at runtime: variables, arrays, objects, reference counting, and memory allocation. Originally written by Zeev Suraski and Andi Gutmans (the name is a contraction of their first names) and introduced with PHP […]

title: Stopping PHP2SHELL: How SentinelOne Protects Customers From This Attack Technique
text: Company16 min readOct 21, 2026Stopping PHP2SHELL: How SentinelOne Protects Customers From This Attack Technique Executive SummaryOn October 21, 2026, the PHP project released versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 to fix two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2. The two flaws are known together as PHP2Shell. They were disclosed by the security firms Calif and Wiz and by OpenAI, working with the PHP security team, after AI-assisted auditing turned an out-of-memory weakness that a 2024 audit had flagged but could not prove exploitable into working remote code execution.Both vulnerabilities sit in PHP's memory management and error handling, code that nearly every request touches, and the earliest affected path dates to PHP 5.4.0. An unauthenticated attacker can execute code on the web server or read its process memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys belonging to other requests. On Apache with mod_php, the attack runs before any application code executes, which means an application with no bugs of its own is still exposed. As of October 21, 2026, no verified proof-of-concept code is available publicly. Attack attempts have been observed by Cloudflare after the leak, but no confirmed in-the-wild compromise has yet been reported.While upgrading every PHP runtime remains the primary control, SentinelOne agent detects attackers’ post-exploitation activities. Once an attacker has code execution on the web server process, the behavior that follows web server flaws: execute shell commands, drop and invoke webshells, download and execute custom payloads and outbound connections. On managed hosts, the Singularity™ agent and Singularity AI SIEM detection content look for such behaviors, and Purple AI® can be used to hunt for it during the patching window. The separate memory-disclosure path runs no code on the host, so it leaves no process behavior to detect; that path is instead surfaced through web server, WAF, and CDN telemetry forwarded into AI SIEM.This report details PHP2Shell's mechanism, affected versions, and confirmed activity, and outlines how SentinelOne customers can strengthen their defenses.Key HighlightsThe flaw is in PHP itself, not in any application. WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, Magento, Laravel, and other web applications are all exposed on an affected PHP version, because the vulnerable code is in the runtime beneath them.The patch is the only complete fix. PHP states plainly that no configuration change fully closes the vulnerability. Every interim mitigation reduces one attack path and leaves others open.The unauthenticated path runs before your code does. On Apache with mod_php, a single crafted HTTP request triggers the flaw during request startup, so application-level controls never see it. PHP assesses the risk as highest for mod_php.Memory disclosure leaks secrets without a shell. One path reads live worker memory and returns passwords, tokens, API keys, and certificates with no code execution, which makes it quieter than a shell and harder to catch with execution-focused tooling.End of Life PHP will not get a patch. Organizations running PHP 8.1 and prior will not receive an official release. Source-only backports exist for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, and distribution or LTS vendors may offer fixed packages.Leverage SentinelOne platform post-exploitation coverage. The detection by the agent is agnostic to the vulnerability and exploit chain and focuses on attackers activity following the exploit, including but not limited to, installation and usage of webshells, command executions and outbound connection behavior that follows the code execution.Organizations should take the following steps immediately:Update every PHP runtime to a fixed version and restart Apache, PHP-FPM, and any long-running workers.Inventory internet-facing PHP, including the copies bundled inside appliances, control panels, and vendor software.Isolate end-of-life PHP (8.1 and older) […]

title: 'PHP2Shell' Bugs Signal Red Alert for Security Industry
text: Alexander Culafi,Senior News Writer,Dark ReadingOctober 21, 20264 Min ReadCredit: DSGpro via Getty Images A pair of critical vulnerabilities tied to open source scripting language PHP appear to have significant consequences for much of the server infrastructure holding the Internet afloat.These vulnerabilities, dubbed "php2shell" by some researchers, include CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. CVE-2026-109618 enables remote code execution (RCE) via out-of-memory corruption, and CVE-2026-109619 enables RCE via a stale global state. The vulnerabilities, discovered by infosec consulting firm Calif, were designated with a critical CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2.According to a WatchTowr blog post, both PHP vulnerabilities let an attacker run their own code on a Web server without logging in. "It stems from stale internal data that survives after its memory is freed; a later request handled by the same worker can use that leftover data, and PHP confirms this can let an attacker run their own code on the server without logging in. Reaching the server over the network is enough; no account or prior access is needed," researchers said in the blog post. Patch Your Web-Facing PHP Servers NowOrganizations should update affected servers to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 to protect against the flaws. As 8.2 through 8.5 are the supported versions of PHP, lower numbered versions do not have a patch available, meaning organizations must either upgrade their PHP versions to a supported branch or use a backported fix. PHP's security advisory urges that while only an update is a complete solution, organizations can take certain actions to reduce exposure until that time.PHP's maintainers initially said yesterday that an emergency security release was scheduled for Wednesday at 14:00 UTC alongside coordinated disclosure, but as WatchTowr's blog post explained, the embargo broke. A proof of concept tool called "PHP2Shell" came to light, and WatchTowr claimed to be able to recreate both vulnerabilities. John Hammond, senior principal security researcher for Huntress, tells Dark Reading that there was a silver lining in the leak in that it "pushed defenders to inventory systems, prepare mitigations, and get ready to patch sooner."On the other hand, "that same early warning was available to attackers, who were undoubtedly spinning up AI and LLMs to find the vulnerabilities, identify targets, and start developing or adapting exploits," Hammond adds.This may not be theoretical risk, either; WatchTowr reported it has observed exploitation attempts of both flaws in the wild. Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence for WatchTowr, tells Dark Reading that while no one has been successful yet, the company does not expect this to be the case for very long. The vendor said the potential for exploitation is broad across vulnerable PHP installations, and security teams should prioritize "internet-facing servers running PHP as an Apache module," as the PHP Foundation highlighted that configuration as having the highest risk."Every PHP installation that serves web requests is in scope, including PHP-FPM, Apache’s mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, and PHP says the risk is highest on mod_php, where an attack can succeed before any application code runs," WatchTowr's blog post read. "Session Upload Progress, a feature turned on by default, offers one confirmed path to the problem, so most default deployments meet that precondition."More Critical Bugs Involving Open Source ProjectsPHP is a common, highly supported programming language run on servers across the globe and used for web development. The scope of organizations using PHP spans the Internet, from enterprises to small businesses, critical infrastructure, and municipalities. Many organizations, like the Netherlands' National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), took websites and services down to limit exposure and/or facilitate emergency patching. As the Independent Federated Intelligence Network, a […]

title: Critical GitLab Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Could Allow Unauthenticated RCE Across 12 Years of Releases
text:
Critical GitLab Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Could Allow Unauthenticated RCE Across 12 Years of ReleasesSwati KhandelwalOct 21, 2026Vulnerability / Software Security

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014.

The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier: the October 12 update covered only versions 19.2 and later, and the new fixed versions sit one patch above it, so an instance updated then is in range again.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, is rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale, the maximum. GitLab says that, under certain conditions, it could allow an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code on the server due to an integer overflow during the compilation of a specially crafted regular expression.

GitLab has not said what those conditions are. The company reports no sign the flaw has been used in attacks, and it is not listed in the U.S. CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities as of October 22.

Only self-managed installations need to act. GitLab.com already runs the fixed version, and GitLab Dedicated tenants on the internal releases 19.3.5-internal0 and 19.4.2-internal0 or later already have the fix.

GitLab fixed the flaw in seven versions at once.

The table below pairs each release branch with the version that fixes it.

If you run

Upgrade to

19.5 before 19.5.1

19.5.1

19.4 before 19.4.3

19.4.3

19.3 before 19.3.6

19.3.6

19.2 before 19.2.9

19.2.9

19.1 before 19.1.9

19.1.9

19.0 before 19.0.10

19.0.10

7.0 through 18.11, before 18.11.13

18.11.13

Four of those versions are older than GitLab normally patches. The company's policy covers the current release and the previous two monthly releases, which, as of today, are 19.5, 19.4, and 19.3.

GitLab said it backported this fix to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, and 19.2.9 on top of its standard releases, a step it reserves for severe issues.

The reason the flaw reaches so far back is the part of GitLab that failed. The regular-expression compiler is Ruby's built-in engine, called Onigmo, which GitLab ships inside its own packages and patches in its own builds. A weakness in that engine is present wherever GitLab has shipped it, which is every release since 7.0.

GitLab also published two detection rules to help self-managed administrators look for exploitation attempts, named "Onigmo native worker crash" and "Org mode render error burst." They are part of the company's open-source TLDR framework, which writes each detection in the Sigma format against GitLab's own application logs.

GitLab has not said what preconditions an attacker needs to reach the compiler, so administrators cannot yet rule themselves out by configuration; the fix is the only certain protection, and GitLab's advisory offers no interim workaround.

This is the fourth code-execution flaw in GitLab's regular-expression engine that the same researcher, who uses the handle joaxcar, has reported in a month, and the first to reach versions before 19.2.

On October 12, GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229, also an unauthenticated 10.0 overflow in the regex compiler, in versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2. On September 23, it fixed two more, CVE-2026-93577 and CVE-2026-89078, both rated 9.9 but requiring a logged-in account. The three earlier flaws stopped at version 19.2; this one does not.

The October 21 release fixes 11 security issues in all, one critical and the rest high, medium, or low.

Two of the others concern authentication. CVE-2026-15723, rated high at 8.2, could allow a logged-in user to take over another account, but only when an administrator has enabled both SAML and LDAP auto-linking.

title: PHP2Shell: How to Protect Your Server | Kaspersky official blog
text:
Two critical vulnerabilities have been discovered in the popular PHP programming language. The vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow attackers to remotely execute code on a server running PHP without authentication. The language’s development team has released updates for all supported branches, but the first attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities were observed even before the patches were published. The exploit has been named PHP2Shell.
The architectures of popular marketplaces, e-commerce platforms, and learning management systems (LMS) are written in PHP. In addition, PHP is used in various content management systems (CMS) such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and so on, which power most websites on the internet.
In this blogpost, we discuss CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in detail, and explain how companies can protect their infrastructure. Read the Securelist expert blog to learn how events surrounding these vulnerabilities unfolded before the patch was released.
Vulnerable PHP versions
According to PHP web site, versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12 are vulnerable to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. There are no official fixes for older branches. According to unofficial reports, the vulnerabilities also affect PHP versions starting with 5.4.0.
What makes CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 dangerous
Both vulnerabilities received a score of 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale. They arise because, after a request is interrupted (for example, due to a memory shortage), PHP leaves invalid data in the memory buffer, and subsequently accesses it, allowing code to be executed on the server. One of the confirmed attack chains via CVE-2026-109619 exploits the `session.upload_progress` mechanism (which tracks file upload progress), which is enabled by default in PHP.
By exploiting these vulnerabilities, attackers can remotely execute code on the server with web server process privileges without authentication.
According to PHP developers, all installations of unpatched versions that process web requests are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. The greatest risk lies with mod_php: researchers demonstrated an exploit for it in which an unauthenticated request triggers the attack even before the application code is executed.
What businesses should do
We’ve compiled key recommendations from the PHP developers and experts at Kaspersky.

Update PHP to versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35. Start with systems accessible from the internet. The source code is available on the PHP website. If PHP is installed from distribution packages or provided by your hosting provider, check for updated packages: Linux distributions and LTS vendors received patches in advance. If the server is managed by a hosting provider, ask them to apply the update.
Versions 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Check with your distribution vendor or LTS support provider to see if backported fixes are available, or switch to a supported branch. For PHP 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, the developers have prepared minimal source code backports for manual compilation. These can also be found on the PHP website.
Restart PHP-FPM or the web server so that the processes load the new code, and verify the version using the `php -v` command. If PHP was installed from distribution packages, check the package changelog: the version number may remain the same.
Check the logs from October 20. A warning sign is when the web server process is performing actions it shouldn’t (running command shells, curl, wget, and the like). Kaspersky solutions help detect malicious activity in a timely manner. Attempts to exploit the described RCE vulnerabilities on Linux and Windows machines can be detected using Kaspersky NEXT EDR Expert, while exploitation of PHP2Shell in network traffic is detected by Kaspersky Anti Targeted Attack (KATA) with the NDR module.

title: PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge
text:
PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts EmergeSwati KhandelwalOct 21, 2026Vulnerability / Web Security

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

PHP has released emergency updates that fix two critical flaws in the language itself, letting an attacker without an account run code on a web server. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the PHP team says only updating fully protects a server.

The flaws, together called PHP2Shell, sit in the PHP runtime, not in any application, so a site is exposed even when its own code is secure. The risk is highest on servers using Apache's mod_php, where a working exploit triggers the attack before any application code runs.

Both flaws are rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale and carry the identifiers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. PHP published them around the scheduled release time of 14:00 UTC on October 21, a day after details leaked ahead of a planned October 22 disclosure.

Researchers at Wiz, Calif, and OpenAI found and reported the flaws, which affect nearly every PHP version back to PHP 5.4.

Who Is Affected

Every PHP installation that serves web requests is at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed, according to the PHP security advisory.

Because the flaws are in the engine rather than in any site's code, even a simple "Hello World" page on a vulnerable PHP version can be attacked.

The advisory singles out mod_php as the highest risk, with a demonstrated exploit in which a single unauthenticated request triggers the attack before any application code runs. PHP-FPM behaves differently, because it shuts the worker down when a request fails early in setup.

For one of the two flaws, PHP's own analysis supports that FPM is susceptible but says no complete FPM exploit has been shown; the second flaw was shown to reach code execution on both mod_php and PHP-FPM, though the FPM path there depends on an operation inside the running application.

An attacker can also read memory from the PHP worker process, which may hold passwords, authentication tokens, API keys, and certificates belonging to other requests, without first gaining code execution.

The researchers demonstrated this reading of live worker memory against applications they did not control, making it independent of the application running on top of PHP.

What to Install

Update the PHP runtime that serves web requests, then restart Apache, PHP-FPM, and any long-running PHP workers. Updating an application such as WordPress or Laravel does not update the PHP runtime beneath it; that comes from the server package, the host, or the container image.

below 8.3.36

PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project, and PHP 8.2 reaches end of life on December 31, 2026. For the older branches, the PHP security team has published source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1 to help people building from source or waiting on a vendor.

Linux distributions and long-term-support vendors received the patches in advance, so a distribution package can carry the fix under an old-looking version number; check the package changelog for the CVE, as Debian advises, not the version string.

If You Cannot Update Yet

Only updating is a complete fix. The measures below reduce exposure to specific attack paths and do not make a server safe, according to the advisory.

For CVE-2026-109618, set memory_limit=-1 so applications cannot override it, keep post_max_size low, and enforce request-size limits at the web server or proxy. Do not use RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA as a substitute, because PHP warns they can trigger the same vulnerable […]

title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
text: Today, Calif.io, Wiz, OpenAI and Quarkslab disclosed two vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and known as php2shell. The vulnerabilities affect all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later and they may allow an attacker to cause denial of service, remote code execution, and data exposure when an application processes specially crafted HTTP traffic.Cloudflare has been part of a coordinated effort to deploy mitigations to protect the Internet, working with PHP foundation, OpenAI and Wiz among others. Cloudflare has developed and deployed web application firewall (WAF) protections since early October 2026, which were deployed about 9 hours ahead of public disclosure. Starting on October 21 3:02 am UTC, Cloudflare customers using our free or paid WAF were protected by default against php2shell.Cloudflare successfully deployed multiple mitigations for all its customers while the vulnerability was leaked before the official release date and we observed attack traffic targeting our customers. We observed how attackers were mutating the attack payload to try to bypass our protections by tracking the volume of matches and cross-referencing with the rule logic.Protecting against php2shell required more than standard request-based rules. Request data alone does not always provide enough evidence to distinguish an exploit from legitimate traffic. The origin’s response adds context, helping identify whether an exploit succeeded while reducing the risk of false positives.To deliver this protection, we developed full transaction detection, a new Cloudflare WAF capability that combines signals from the request and response within the same HTTP transaction. Response rules can then block a matching origin response before it reaches the requester. The php2shell protections are the first managed detections we have released using this capability.Customers should patch their PHP repos even with WAF protections providing an additional layer of defense-in-depth mitigation. Our security analysts continue monitoring attack activity and update the rules when and if new techniques and variations emerge in the hours and days ahead. You can track new rules in the changelog.The protections are available and deployed automatically on all plans with WAF deployed, including Free users.Copy linkWhat we know about the vulnerabilitiesPHP is used by almost 70% of websites. The php2shell vulnerabilities affect the PHP runtime itself and can allow attackers to execute malicious code on vulnerable servers, expose customer data, or disrupt services. Because PHP underpins widely used platforms such as WordPress and Magento, these flaws could potentially affect a large number of applications across the Internet.The two vulnerabilities involve how PHP handles memory when something goes wrong while processing a HTTP request. Normally, PHP allocates memory to store the data it needs to process a request, then releases it when that work finishes. If processing stops unexpectedly, for example because it runs out of memory, PHP fails to clean up the memory safely. These vulnerabilities arise when PHP handles an error and then tries to use data that was not fully set up or memory that has already been released.An attacker can send specially crafted HTTP requests to trigger these conditions. Large requests are one way to put memory under pressure, but the problem goes beyond consuming server resources. By manipulating the data PHP encounters in this invalid memory, an attacker may be able to crash a PHP process, expose sensitive information, or execute code provided by the attacker.The two vulnerabilities differ in when the unsafe memory access happens:VulnerabilityWhat goes wrongCVE-2026-109618PHP runs out of memory and interrupts its work before some internal data has been properly initialized. During cleanup of that request, PHP may use this unfinished data as though it were valid.CVE-2026-109619A fatal error interrupts a request, leaving PHP […]

title: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
text:
PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn'tSwati KhandelwalOct 21, 2026Vulnerability / Server Security

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

You cannot fully block the two critical PHP flaws called PHP2Shell before today's fix, and the one setting being passed around as a workaround is not enough on its own, the security firm that suggested it now says.

PHP will release the fix at 14:00 UTC on October 21 for two flaws it rates 9.2 out of 10, and has given no workaround of its own. Until you can install it, what lowers your risk is taking exposed PHP off the internet or behind access controls, cutting what a compromised server can reach, and having the update ready to apply the moment it lands.

Cloudflare says it is seeing early attempts to exploit the flaws, and has pushed emergency rules for sites behind it that it calls a stopgap until you patch. No compromise has been confirmed, the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work, and neither flaw is in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws.PHP has not said which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, or whether any setting changes the risk; it says the full details and the fixed versions come with the release.

⚡ UPDATE — PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge

At the time of writing, that release was not yet out. So nobody outside the group that found the flaws can test whether a given defense works, which is why the advice below is about lowering risk, not promising safety.

The setting you were told to change is not protection

The workaround spreading on social media and security blogs is one line in a PHP configuration file: session.upload_progress.enabled=0. It turns off Session Upload Progress, a PHP feature that's enabled by default, which records how far a file upload has progressed so another request can check on it.

GMO Flatt Security, a Tokyo security firm, suggested setting it early on October 21, saying it could not be sure the change fully addresses the flaws but thought it would help with some probability.

Later the same day, the firm walked that back. In an update timestamped 14:00 Japan time (05:00 UTC), it said the setting alone is not a complete fix and that attacks getting around it are expected. It told administrators to prepare their update, watch for attack traffic before the release, and apply the fix as soon as it is out.

Two people from the PHP project said the same thing more bluntly. Replying to someone who suggested the upload-progress setting might patch the flaw, Gina Peter Banyard, a PHP core developer and documentation writer funded by the PHP Foundation, wrote: "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP. I sadly know too much." Joe Ferguson, the release manager for the coming PHP 8.6, put it shorter: "ini settings won't save you."

The setting cannot be relied on for two reasons. GMO Flatt expects a way around it but has not said what that is. And the whole idea that the flaw lives in Session Upload Progress is a guess: PHP has not confirmed it, the firm itself said it holds only so far as its own research matches PHP2Shell, and an independent code audit argues the specific bug others describe in that feature does not exist in released PHP. That audit is from an anonymous account and PHP's own code will settle it, but it is one more reason not to treat the setting as a shield.

Not everyone agrees. One vendor, Upwind, still lists the setting as an immediate mitigation, passing along another researcher's analysis rather than its own tests. watchTowr, which reproduced one of the flaws, says there is "no confirmed patch or workaround at this time."

If you already set it

No one is telling you to undo the […]

title: Attackers Abuse UpdraftCentral Keys to Plant Backdoors on WordPress Sites
text:
Attackers Abuse UpdraftCentral Keys to Plant Backdoors on WordPress SitesRavie LakshmananOct 21, 2026Cyber Attack / Web Security

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

Unknown threat actors breached TeamUpdraft's website and potentially gained unauthorized access to customers' connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone, using them to backdoor WordPress sites.

TeamUpdraft is the developer behind UpdraftPlus, a popular WordPress backup plugin with over four million active installations. The vendor also offers UpdraftCentral, a remote management service that's used for managing multiple sites remotely. A client component of UpdraftCentral is shipped within every copy of UpdraftPlus.

"Over the weekend of 17-18 October we identified unauthorized access to the teamupdraft.com website," TeamUpdraft said in a statement. "Our team responded straight away and worked through the night to contain it – we closed the access route, signed out every account and replaced the keys and credentials that could have been affected."

As a result of the incident, threat actors are believed to have accessed its customer database, which holds the following information -

Names, email addresses, billing addresses and order history
Account passwords, stored only in hashed (scrambled) form and never in plain text
Two-factor authentication (2FA) settings
Connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone

TeamUpdraft said the database does not hold any financial information, and that they are handled by Stripe and PayPal. It also emphasized that the UpdraftPlus plugin, along with self-hosted versions of UpdraftCentral and backups sent to customers' own remote storage, are not impacted.

"However, if your site was accessed through UpdraftCentral, please also re-authorise your remote storage and change any storage access keys, as a precaution," it said.

In addition, TeamUpdraft said it deployed a fix to address the underlying issue, signed out every teamupdraft.com account and reset login security across the site, and released UpdraftPlus 1.26.13 (free) and 2.26.13 (Premium) to automatically disconnect every UpdraftCentral connection made before 10 p.m. BST on October 18, 2026, to prevent the old keys from working.

Other steps taken by the developer are listed below -

Disconnected every site from UpdraftVault and issued new credentials
Replaced every UpdraftClone client key
Rotated its keys with payment providers and other connected services
Implemented additional monitoring in place
Reported the incident to the U.K. Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and other relevant authorities

Users who have a teamupdraft.com account are advised to change their password with immediate effect (and elsewhere, if the same password has been reused), reset 2FA settings, and exercise caution when receiving unexpected emails claiming to be from TeamUpdraft.

TeamUpdraft is also recommending that cloud customers of UpdraftCentral follow the steps below as soon as possible, since the connection keys can send commands to the connected sites -

Log in to the site's own WordPress dashboard, not through UpdraftCentral.
Update UpdraftPlus to version 1.26.12 (free) or 2.26.12 (Premium) or later.
Disconnect it from UpdraftCentral: go to Settings > UpdraftPlus > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral and delete the connection key.
Go to Users and check for any administrator accounts you don’t recognise. Remove them.
Go to Plugins, including the Must-Use tab if you can see it, and check for anything you don’t recognise. Remove it.
Change the passwords for all administrator accounts on the site.
If you find anything suspicious, consider restoring the site from a backup taken before 17 October.
Reconnect the site to UpdraftCentral.

UpdraftVault users are being urged to reconnect their […]

text:
PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security AlertSwati KhandelwalOct 21, 2026Vulnerability / Web Security

//<![CDATA[

//]]>

This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory.

PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described.

⚡ UPDATE — PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge

Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far.

The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'".

watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now.

PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."

The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale.

The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described.

PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's.

Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches, and records each branch's changes in its changelog. Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support. Ahead of the release, several trackers, including Alpine Linux's and security researcher Kevin Beaumont, expect the fixes to ship as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the next point release of each branch, though PHP has not confirmed the numbers.

Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch.

Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10.
Waiting for PHP2Shell
“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”
The maintainers published the advisory following the leaking of purported details, which have yet to be confirmed. The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running:

WordPress 7.1.3
MediaWiki 1.46.2
phpBB 3.3.17
Magento 2.4.9
Joomla 6.2.0
Laravel 13.36.0
Laravel 8.83.29
Symphony 8.1.9
Drupal 11.4.10
WHMCS 9.0.9

All of the above use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here.
Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.

Researchers from another security firm, Sansec, said they “expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release.” A third security firm, Webfence, also urged admins to prepare now. Huntress has also issued an advisory.
Preparation steps include identifying who is responsible for managing PHP inside an organization, taking an inventory of every app built on the language, planning a maintenance window starting at 14:00 UTC with contingency plans for moving earlier, making a backup of site and database files, and monitoring the PHP.net homepage for any late-breaking announcements, including an earlier release time. Some experts suggest unplugging any nonessential systems until they’re patched.
As an open source scripting language for building dynamic websites and web apps, PHP has come to be a de facto building block for the Web. It runs multiple CMS apps in addition to WordPress and also powers many internal tools. One security researcher said an estimated 1.3 million Internet-connected hosts are likely affected. Vulnerabilities with the severity the advisories are describing have the potential to inflict major damage across the Internet. Admins should remain aware that the patches can be released at any moment and remain vigilant until they are.
Update: Source file fixes were added to the php-src Github repo at 13:34 UTC this morning, with advisories here and here. Packages and docker images have begun filtering out as maintainers get their hands on the new sources. Our advice is unchanged from earlier: update as soon as possible.

CVE-2026-112408 - Missing bucket ownership verification in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK default_bucket()

Bulletin ID: 2026-142-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 10/21/2026 12:30 PM PDT

Description:

The Amazon SageMaker Python SDK is an open-source library for training and deploying machine learning models on Amazon SageMaker. We identified CVE-2026-112408, an issue in the default_bucket() function. The SDK uses a predictably named Amazon S3 bucket and does not check that the caller's AWS account owns it. A remote actor who creates that bucket first could achieve code execution in a remote SageMaker execution environment and obtain IAM credentials.

Impacted versions:

V2: < 2.257.3
V3: >= 3.0.0 and < 3.10.0

Resolution:

This issue has been addressed in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK versions 2.257.3 (V2) and 3.10.0 (V3). We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.

Workarounds:

If you are not able to upgrade, pass an S3 bucket that your account owns explicitly through the default_bucket parameter of sagemaker.Session (or through the SageMaker SDK configuration file). Do not rely on the auto-generated default bucket name.

References:

CVE-2026-112408
GHSA-5rx8-8fr2-f855

Acknowledgement:

We would like to thank Dan Gansel from Upwind Security for collaborating on this issue through the coordinated disclosure process.

PHP web runtimes (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)

Bulletin ID: 2026-143-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 10/21/2026 14:30 PM PDT

Summary:

Two critical issues have been identified in PHP web runtimes (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that can allow an unauthenticated actor to run code on affected systems. A remote caller can send crafted web requests to affected PHP workers and execute arbitrary code, read process-accessible data, or cause denial of service.

AWS services are not impacted by these issues. Customers using the affected versions of PHP within the services listed below could be impacted and should review the guidance provided.

Affected versions:

PHP 8.5: Affected versions 8.5.0–8.5.11 · First fixed version: 8.5.12
PHP 8.4: Affected versions 8.4.0–8.4.26 · First fixed version: 8.4.27
PHP 8.3: Affected versions 8.3.0–8.3.35 · First fixed version: 8.3.36
PHP 8.2: Affected versions 8.2.0–8.2.34 · First fixed version: 8.2.35
PHP 5.4–8.1: No upstream fix released. End-of-life and have no planned fix. Migration to a supported branch is required.

Impact:

This issue is accessible remotely by an actor without authentication over the internet-to-customer-application boundary, which can result in code execution, unintended access to process-accessible data, or denial of service on the targeted PHP worker. The issue is bounded to the affected worker and its application-level permissions; no cross-customer propagation has been established to date.

Current Mitigation Status:

Amazon WorkMail: AWS has applied configuration-level controls that limit the conditions under which these issues can be reached. The upgrade to PHP 8.3.36 is targeted for 2026-10-22. No customer action is required.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk: AWS released updated PHP platform versions (v4.13.12) on 2026-10-21 that address both CVEs. A follow-on platform release containing the upstream PHP fix is targeted for 2026-10-22. Customers with Managed Platform Updates enabled will receive the update automatically during their next maintenance window. Customers who have not enabled Managed Platform Updates should update their environment's platform version by following the documentation.

Amazon Linux: Updated PHP packages are targeted for 2026-10-22. Customers running PHP on Amazon Linux should apply the updated packages as soon as they are available. Please follow CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in the Amazon Linux Security Center for details.

Amazon Lightsail: Updated Lightsail blueprints are expected on 2026-10-21. AWS cannot update running Lightsail instances in place. Customers running PHP workloads on Lightsail should create new instances from the updated blueprints and migrate their applications following the documentation.

Mitigation Guidance:

Upgrading immediately to a patched PHP release is the only complete fix: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35. The configuration changes below may reduce impact for customers who cannot update immediately, but none is a complete mitigation.

All PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed are considered at risk. Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could allow for unauthenticated remote code execution in the context of the affected service account. Depending on the privileges associated with the service account, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Services whose accounts are configured to have less rights on the system could be less impacted than those who operate with administrative user rights.THREAT INTELLIGENCE:While there are currently no reports of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, the potential for exploitation is a high risk. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. (CVE-2026-109618)RCE via stale global state: request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. (CVE-2026-109619)Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could allow for unauthenticated remote code execution in the context of the affected service account. Depending on the privileges associated with the service account, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Services whose accounts are configured to have less rights on the system could be less impacted than those who operate with administrative user rights.RECOMMENDATIONS:We recommend the following actions be taken:If you cannot update immediately: While only an update is a complete solution, the following measures reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe:RCE via OOM corruption (CVE-2026-109618): Set memory_limit=-1, preferably in a way applications can't override, such as php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration, and check that no pool, directory or application setting puts a finite limit back. Critical PHP Vulnerability (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) [infocon yellow]

2 comment(s)

PHP.net announced that it will release a critical update today. We decided to change the infoCon to YELLOW due to the widespread use of PHP, the expected severity of the flaw (CVSS 9.4), and the availability of early PoC exploits before the patch became available.

Various vendors have released bulletins listing products that must be patched for this vulnerability. For example:

Cisco  https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-php-october26-Jj384Daq
OPNSense https://x.com/opnsense/status/2112985458514756087
PFSense https://forum.netgate.com/topic/201565/critical-php-security-update
Palo Alto Networks https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618

Many open source firewall/router products use PHP. Expect updates for them, and as always, do not expose the web admin interface to the internet.

PHP also published a summary around the release:

https://thephp.foundation/blog/2026/10/21/todays-php-security-release-and-how-were-strengthening-php-security/

The PHP update was released as scheduled: https://www.php.net/index.php#2026-10-20-1

This diary will be continuously updated today. I am starting to write this diary with many details still unclear and with the patch not yet available.

Which versions of PHP are vulnerable?

The easy answer: All of them. At least starting with PHP 5, including the most recent releases.

PHP Versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, all released today, are currently the only "safe" versions. Note that Linux distributions may backport the patch for older versions.

Ubuntu just released updated PHP packages for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, 26.04, and  26.10. [ubuntu].

Which versions will receive patches?

Only PHP 8 is expected to receive a patch. Older versions are no longer supported. The patch is expected to be released at 14:00 UTC today, October 21st. [php] Ubuntu will release patches "as soon as possible" and may include backported patches for PHP versions included in supported Ubuntu versions.

The real "race to patch" does not start at 14:00 UTC for most people, but at the time distributions release updated packages. Most PHP sites do not use PHP compiled from php.net directly. It will almost certainly be faster to wait for your distribution to release an update.

Does this vulnerability affect specific configurations or extensions?

The vulnerability is in the PHP core, and all default PHP installations are expected to be vulnerable (see below for mitigations).

What steps can I take to mitigate the vulnerability before applying the patch?

Early guidance suggests that the configuration setting "session.upload_progress.enabled = Off" provides partial mitigation against the vulnerability being exploited. By default, this setting is "On". Restricting the maximum allowed request size in your web server and/or PHP configuration may also help.

Are there WAF rules or other measures to protect a site running PHP?

Yes. I will add more as I verify them. Cloudflare appears to have already deployed some protections. Other vendors have likely done the same.

Have exploits been seen "in the wild"?

Cloudflare is reporting exploits [cloudflare]. PoC exploits and vulnerability details have been released [jackalsyn]

How do the vulnerabilities work?

Wiz Security published a blog post detailing how they discovered the vulnerability using AI tools. [wiz]

title: php2shell: Assessing Elastic detection coverage relevant to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
text: Threat Commandphp2shell: Assessing Elastic detection coverage relevant to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are critical PHP core RCE flaws that leaked ahead of disclosure. We cover what is verified, why exploitation converges on a web server spawning a shell, and the Elastic detections developed to catch this behavior.October 21, 2026Ruben GroenewoudBryan Porras BlanchDetection EngineeringThreat IntelligenceJump to Share On October 20, 2026, details of two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, leaked online ahead of their coordinated disclosure and before any patch existed. The PHP security team responded with advance notice of an emergency security release, scheduled for October 21, 2026 at 14:00 UTC, and rated both flaws critical with a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. Researchers at watchTowr confirmed the vulnerabilities are real and said they reproduced CVE-2026-109618, while noting they have not observed in-the-wild exploitation. The nickname circulating among researchers is php2shell.PHP runs behind a very large share of the web: WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento, shared hosting and control panels, and a long tail of vendor software that bundles a PHP runtime without advertising it. When a critical bug lands in PHP core rather than in one application on top of it, the number of places you have to inventory grows quickly.The PHP security team and the reporting researchers have now published the technical root cause, a pair of memory-safety bugs in PHP core, but at the time of writing there is still no reliable public proof-of-concept to run end to end. That is an awkward position for a defender, because you cannot simply run the exploit and watch the rules fire. It is not, however, a blind spot. An RCE in a PHP web application ends in the same observable place: a PHP worker process doing something a PHP worker process should not do. That convergent behavior is what we detect, and it is what this post is about.In this post, we will cover:What the advisory confirmed about CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and what it means for defenders.Why php2shell will likely behave like generic PHP backend exploitation.The convergent post-exploitation flow, and the Elastic rules that cover this behavior.How to assess and prepare potential coverage before the PoC lands, and what to do right now.We have walked a PHP-adjacent RCE end-to-end before, in Detecting wp2shell: WordPress pre-authentication RCE in the wild, which turned out to use the same precedence and was caught through similar pre-built behavioral rules.What we know about CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619Here is what is verified at the time of writing, and what is not.What we know. Both vulnerabilities are unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in PHP core, each rated critical by the PHP security team with a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. They were reported by Wiz Research, which identified them with the help of frontier AI models and coordinated disclosure with the PHP project. Additionally, a web page called php2shell was created and contains a lot of relevant information about the vulnerability. Information leaked on October 20 ahead of the embargo, which is why PHP moved its release forward to October 21 at 14:00 UTC. With that release, PHP published the patched versions, the affected branches, and the technical root cause.The PHP security team patched the vulnerabilities through commit 31c0ea7d7ff1d1fccb6492e52dab544011628065.What we do not know.
